hint: HO-0820 sewer backup, house empty for months

expected.why: Vacant from 2 April to 22 July (more than 60 consecutive days): E-52 suspends the HO-0820 water backup coverage, so E-16 excludes the backup.

notes: CLM-2024-20061. DOL 2024-07-22. HO-3 with HO-0304 ed. 03-24 and HO-0820 ed. 05-24 attached. Insured Mr. Tobias Wren has been living with his daughter abroad since 2 April and the house has stood empty since then. After a storm on 22 July the floor drain backed up and a neighbour found sewage across the finished basement. Contractor estimate 8,600. Insured asks us to confirm the water backup cover pays. Excess 1,000.

hint: DP-0703 rental, burst pipe in January between tenants

expected.why: Heat was switched off in January (November-March): E-62 excludes water damage of any kind absolutely. E-61 is not the issue - the unit was empty only 11 days.

notes: CLM-2025-20062. DOL 2025-01-14. Dwelling fire DP-3 on a rental house, DP-0703 ed. 02-24 attached. Tenant moved out on 3 January. The owner, Ms. Hannah Kerr, turned the heating off to save money while she looked for a new tenant. The kitchen supply line froze and burst on 14 January and was found the next morning. The house had been empty only 11 days, well under the 30 in E-61. Excess 500.

hint: HO-0612 fire rebuild, city demands lead paint abatement

expected.why: Lead paint abatement and air monitoring are pollutant remediation, testing and monitoring: E-41 excludes them absolutely, even though the ordinance requires them.

notes: CLM-2024-20063. DOL 2024-08-09. HO-3 with HO-0612 ed. 03-24, Coverage A 300,000. Kitchen fire. The city will not issue the rebuild permit until lead paint is abated in the undamaged rooms and air monitoring is done, quote 6,200. Insured Dr. Samuel Achebe says the ordinance or law cover was raised to 25 percent and should pay it. Excess 1,000.

hint: HO-0415 hail dents on a metal roof, no leaks

expected.why: Denting of a metal roof without loss of water-shedding function: E-22 excludes it absolutely.

notes: CLM-2024-20065. DOL 2024-06-03. HO-3 with HO-0415 ed. 01-24. A hail storm on 3 June dented the metal roof panels across the south slope. The roofer confirms there are no leaks and no split seams and the panels still shed water, but insured Mr. Kevin Mbeki, phone (555) 301-7788, says the house now looks run down and wants every panel replaced, quote 18,400. Excess 2,500.

hint: HO-0304 toilet supply fitting 'let go', plumber says it wept for weeks

expected.why: The plumber puts the discharge at about three weeks before discovery - over the 14 days in Clause 1(a), so it is not sudden and accidental: the E-17 exception fails and E-18 continuous seepage excludes it.

notes: CLM-2024-20066. DOL 2024-09-12. HO-3 with HO-0304 ed. 03-24. The compression fitting on the supply line to the upstairs toilet let go and insured Mrs. Joan Pell found the ceiling below soaked on 12 September. The plumber's report says the fitting had been weeping for around three weeks before it failed completely. Insured kept the fitting. Excess 1,000.

hint: HO-0820 sump pump stopped in a 5-hour power cut, dead battery backup

expected.why: The battery backup was never replaced and the pump never tested - a failure to keep the sump pump in working order. The power outage was about 5 hours, under the 12 continuous hours the E-51 exception needs.

notes: CLM-2024-20067. DOL 2024-04-18. HO-3 with HO-0820 ed. 05-24. A storm knocked the power out for about 5 hours; the sump pump stopped and the basement took water. The battery backup unit was dead - insured Mr. Liam Ortega admits it has never been replaced since he bought the house in 2019 and the pump has never been tested. Insured says the power cut is not his fault. Excess 1,000.

hint: HO-0820 sewer backup, insured moved into a care home, house up for sale

expected.why: Nobody has lived there since 28 February; the backup was on 6 May - 68 days. Showings by an estate agent are not occupancy, so E-52 (vacant more than 60 consecutive days) suspends the HO-0820 coverage and E-16 excludes the backup.

notes: CLM-2024-20070. DOL 2024-05-06. HO-3 with HO-0304 ed. 03-24 and HO-0820 ed. 05-24 attached. Insured Mr. Arthur Penn moved into a care home on 28 February and the house is unfurnished and listed for sale; the estate agent shows it about twice a month. During a storm on 6 May the floor drain backed up and the agent found sewage in the basement. Estimate 7,900. Family asks if the water backup endorsement pays. Excess 1,000.

hint: DP-0703 rental, water shut off and drained, landlord abroad

expected.why: Empty 49 days (over 30). The shut-off-and-drain exception would save it, but Clause 4 says failure to inspect within 7 days of the tenancy ending voids that exception - and no inspection was done. E-61 applies.

notes: CLM-2024-20071. DOL 2024-10-20. Dwelling fire DP-3 rental, DP-0703 ed. 02-24 attached. The tenant left on 1 September. The landlord, Mr. Omar Haddad, lives abroad; he had a plumber shut the water off at the main and drain the system on 3 September (receipt on file). Nobody has been inside since, and no inspection of the unit was done after the tenant left. On 20 October a neighbour reported water coming from under the door - a fitting on the supply line had burst. Excess 500.

hint: DP-0703 rental between tenants in February, thermostat turned down

expected.why: The thermostat was set to 45 degrees F in February - below the 55 degrees F E-62 requires from November to March. E-62 excludes water damage of any kind, absolutely. The 20-day vacancy is under E-61's 30, which is a distraction.

notes: CLM-2025-20072. DOL 2025-02-18. Dwelling fire DP-3 on a rental house, DP-0703 ed. 02-24 attached. Between tenants since 29 January; the owner, Ms. Grace Liu, set the thermostat to 45 degrees to keep the bills down but kept the water on. A pipe in the exterior wall froze and split on 18 February and the kitchen and hall were flooded. Unit empty 20 days. Excess 500.

hint: HO-0820 sump pump, overnight power cut, old battery backup

expected.why: The battery backup was last replaced in 2016 and the pump never tested - failure to keep it in working order. Power was off from 9:30 pm to 7:00 am, 9.5 hours - under the 12 continuous hours the E-51 exception needs.

notes: CLM-2024-20073. DOL 2024-09-27. HO-3 with HO-0820 ed. 05-24. Storm on 26 September: power went off at 9:30 pm and came back at 7:00 am. With no power the sump pump stopped and the battery backup, last replaced in 2016, ran flat within minutes; the basement took 20 cm of water. Insured Mrs. Ruth Calloway says she has never tested the pump. Excess 1,000.

hint: HO-3 + HO-0304 on the insured's home; burst hose at a flat they let out

expected.why: The loss is at a tenant-occupied flat across town, not the residence premises the HO-3 and HO-0304 cover, so the E-17 sudden-and-accidental exception is not the insured's cover here. A rental needs a dwelling-fire policy - and under DP-0703, E-61 would exclude it anyway: empty 38 days, water left on. Right answer: not covered under these forms (NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS or DENIED, naming the missing rental form).

notes: CLM-2024-20074. DOL 2024-12-09. HO-3 on the insured's own home, with HO-0304 ed. 03-24 attached. The loss is at a flat the insured owns across town and lets to tenants: it had been empty 38 days between tenancies, with the water left on, when the washing machine supply hose split. The letting agent found it the next morning. Insured Ms. Nadia Brooks asks us to pay it as a sudden and accidental burst. Excess 1,000.

hint: HO-3 + HO-0820 on the insured's home; sewer backup at a duplex they rent to students

expected.why: The backup is at a rental duplex across town, not the residence premises the HO-3 and its HO-0820 endorsement cover. Even on HO-0820's own terms, the unit had been empty since 1 June - 75 days by 15 August - and E-52 suspends the backup cover beyond 60. Right answer: not covered (NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS or DENIED).

notes: CLM-2024-20075. DOL 2024-08-15. HO-3 on the insured's home with HO-0304 ed. 03-24 and HO-0820 ed. 05-24 attached. The sewer backup was at a duplex the insured owns on the other side of town and rents to students; the lower unit had been empty since 1 June. The floor drain there backed up on 15 August, estimate 6,400. Insured Mr. Felix Grant asks us to confirm the 10,000 backup cover. Excess 1,000.

hint: HO-3 + HO-0304 on the insured's home; burst supply line at a townhouse they rent out elsewhere

expected.why: The loss is at a rental townhouse in another town, not the residence premises the HO-3 and HO-0304 cover, so HO-0304's E-17 exception does not reach it; the rental needs a dwelling-fire policy, which is not on file - and under DP-0703, E-61 would exclude it anyway (empty 52 days, water left on). Right answer: NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS naming the missing rental form.

notes: CLM-2024-20076. DOL 2024-11-18. Insured's HO-3 covers their own home, HO-0304 ed. 03-24 attached. The loss is at a townhouse the insured, Mr. Daniel Reyes, owns in another town and rents out; it stood empty 52 days between tenants and the water was left on when a toilet supply line burst. Excess 1,000.
